Render-Path Unification — Wave 2: Astro SSR-to-HTML parity

Epic task: portabledoc-blog-epic-goal · Charter: .claude/workflows/bp-portabledoc-render-unification-charter.md · Design paper: /papers/perfect-portabledoc-blog-next-astro-phoenix · Wave 1 landed: PR #3449 (grade A−).

The wish (verbatim)

Advance the render-path-unification epic per the charter's W2: SSR the canonical @barkpark/react type-keyed PortableDoc (shipped in W1) into an Astro surface via set:html with NO hydration, then re-run the same DOM-shape cross-surface parity from Astro's BUILD output using the EXISTING golden harness + comparator (reuse them as-is — pc-w4 parity gate + the 91-block golden mirror). Do NOT re-author the block array — the golden mirror is canonical; the Elixir compose.ex output is the source of truth the JS must match 1:1. Prove byte/DOM-shape parity between Astro-SSR'd HTML and the golden. Watch the shared-chunk bundle size if the Astro island budget is tight. Respect verify-only for anything already landed on origin/main.

Where the wave actually stands (reconciled with origin/main)

  • Wave 1 is fully landed (#3449). @barkpark/react exports both PortableDoc({value}) (React component) and renderPortableDocument(value): string (raw HTML string) from BOTH index.ts and server.ts (RSC-safe, context-free). Proven shape-equal to the Elixir :article golden for all 42 non-plugin types.
  • The golden harness already exists and is reusable as-is. Fixtures live at js/packages/react/tests/fixtures/pd-golden/*.golden.json — each carries input (one block), expectedHtml, and a node-for-node shape projection (tag / class-set / data-* / style / text), generated by mix barkpark.portable_doc.gen_pd_parity. DO NOT hand-edit or re-author them — they are the canonical Elixir-sourced source of truth.
  • The Layer-2 DOM-shape comparator already exists at js/packages/react/tests/support/dom-shape.ts (assertShapeEqual / diffShape / parseShape, over happy-dom). It whitespace-collapses, drops pure-whitespace text nodes, treats classes as an order-insensitive set, and compares style-attribute + data-* + text recursively. It has an 8-case non-vacuous-green self-proof. This is exactly the comparator W2 re-runs against Astro output.
  • No W2 / Astro work has landed on origin/main. The only .astro files in the tree are templates/astro-starter/** (foreign-owned by the site-spawner session — OFF LIMITS) and copies inside worktrees. So W2 is a genuine BUILD, not verify-only.

Direction for this wave

The finished W2 experience is a green parity gate that proves an Astro static build emits, for all 42 non-plugin block types, HTML whose DOM shape equals the Elixir golden — with zero client JavaScript shipped. Concretely:

  1. The consumer contract we are validating is the real one. An Astro .astro page imports renderPortableDocument (or PortableDoc) from the built @barkpark/react package, calls it in frontmatter (Node, at build time), and injects the string via set:html with no client directive. This is the exact pattern a real Astro blog would use for Phoenix-faithful static output. Because both W1's renderToStaticMarkup(PortableDoc) and W2's renderPortableDocument() call the SAME emitter, the interesting question is NOT "does the renderer work" — it is "does Astro's build pipeline pass the injected HTML through unchanged?" Astro defaults to compressHTML: true and runs its own compiler/HTML pipeline; the wave must prove the built .html file still shape-matches the golden after Astro touches it.
  2. Reuse, do not re-author. The Astro page reads the SAME pd-golden/*.golden.json fixtures at build time (frontmatter can import the fixtures dir), renders each block, and writes them into the static output. The parity re-run then loads Astro's BUILT HTML, extracts each block fragment, and feeds it through the UNCHANGED assertShapeEqual against each golden's shape/expectedHtml. Zero new goldens, zero comparator changes if the comparator already suffices.
  3. Zero hydration is the whole point — and it makes the bundle worry mostly moot. With set:html + no client directive, Astro ships NO JS island for the rendered content, so the ~16KB gzipped shared renderer chunk (the W1 structural note) is a BUILD-time cost only, never shipped to the browser. The wave should PROVE this (assert the built output ships no PortableDoc JS) rather than merely assert bundle budgets. If any island JS leaks, that is the real finding.
  4. Minimal, throwaway, isolated. The Astro surface is a test-only fixture under the parity harness — NOT templates/astro-starter (foreign-owned), NOT shipped in the published package files (dist only). It needs its own package.json + astro.config; it must slot into the pnpm workspace + turbo pipeline without breaking install/publish/CI. Placement is a key open question for the survey. Because we never hydrate, the Astro @astrojs/react integration is very likely UNNECESSARY — we call a pure string function, so vanilla Astro may suffice, avoiding a heavy React-integration dependency. Confirm this.
  5. Quality bar (Kinsta/Vercel). Beyond the green gate, the seed of a "perfect Astro blog surface": the page should link the shipped @barkpark/react/paper-surface.css exports subpath (proving the consumable-asset path works from Astro), render visually faithful, and ship as pure static HTML with zero JS. That is the aesthetic north star; the parity gate is the correctness floor.

Leaning (tentative — Decide finalizes after two explore rounds): minimal vanilla-Astro test package under js/packages/react/ (or a sibling js/parity/astro/), building via a real astro build to honor the wish's "from Astro's BUILD output"; parity re-run as a vitest suite that shells the build once then asserts against the existing goldens; explicitly assert zero shipped JS. Survey both the full-build path and the Astro Container API (experimental_AstroContainer) so Decide can weigh build-fidelity vs CI weight.

Survey plan (this Strategize phase)

Wide net — width is cheap now; Digest distills. Each surveyor answers one concrete question and reports files/claims/seams.

  • astro-consume-contract — How exactly does an Astro .astro page import + call renderPortableDocument from @barkpark/react and inject via set:html? Does frontmatter run at build time in Node? Why: this is the core W2 seam.
  • astro-html-fidelity — Does Astro's build pipeline (default compressHTML: true, its compiler) mutate HTML injected via set:html in ways that change DOM SHAPE (not just whitespace)? What survives, what doesn't? Why: decides whether the existing comparator suffices or needs a normalization tweak.
  • comparator-reuse-fit — Read tests/support/dom-shape.ts + PortableDoc.parity.test.tsx fully. Can the comparator ingest Astro's built HTML unchanged, or does extracting per-block fragments from a full page need a small harness shim? Why: quantifies the "reuse as-is" claim.
  • golden-fixture-consumption — Map the exact pd-golden/*.golden.json schema (input/expectedHtml/shape/type) and how the Astro page would iterate all 42 at build time. Any fixtures that resist static import? Why: confirms no re-authoring is needed.
  • astro-container-api — Does Astro's experimental_AstroContainer (astro/container) let us render a component to a string in a vitest test WITHOUT a full build? Version/stability? Why: a lighter alternative to a full build for Decide to weigh against the wish's "BUILD output".
  • astro-react-integration-needed — Since we NEVER hydrate, is @astrojs/react required at all, or can vanilla Astro call a pure string function + set:html? Node/React-19 compat constraints? Why: dependency-weight decision for the throwaway surface.
  • workspace-placement — Read js/pnpm-workspace.yaml, root turbo.json, and the react package's files/publish config. Where can a test-only Astro package live so it (a) doesn't publish, (b) doesn't break turbo build/install, (c) is reachable by CI? Why: placement is the biggest structural risk.
  • js-ci-gate — What CI workflow runs the JS gate (.github/workflows/*), what commands, and would adding an astro build + parity vitest step fit the existing Node gate timing/deps? Does the api Elixir gate ever fire for a js-only PR? Why: the PR must merge on its own Node gate.
  • zero-js-proof — How to assert an Astro static build ships ZERO client JS for the rendered content? Inspect dist/ for script tags / island hydration markers. Why: proving "no hydration" is a first-class W2 deliverable, not an afterthought.
  • bundle-size-seam — Read js/packages/react/.size-limit.json (index 18KB / server 17KB). Does W2 change any shipped bundle, or is the ~16KB chunk purely build-time under set:html? What does "Astro island budget" even mean when there is no island? Why: the wish flags bundle size; clarify whether it's real here.
  • paper-surface-css-from-astro — Can the Astro page consume @barkpark/react/paper-surface.css via the exports subpath (link/import) for visual parity? Why: the Kinsta/Vercel quality bar + validates the W1 consumable-asset path end-to-end.
  • elixir-golden-freshness — Is the mix barkpark.portable_doc.gen_pd_parity generator + its 3-mirror freshness lock still green on main? Are the JS fixtures byte-identical to what the current Elixir emitter produces? Why: W2 parity is only meaningful if the golden is current (READ-ONLY — never edit compose.ex).
  • epic-task-ledger — List all 10 children of portabledoc-blog-epic-goal with status; is there already a W2/Astro child task, or does Decide file one? Any stale claims? Why: reconcile the ledger before fan-out.
  • prior-astro-parity-art — Search bp papers/tasks + the tree for ANY prior Astro-render or SSR-parity attempt (site-spawner, search-template, web fork). What's reusable, what collides? Why: avoid re-inventing; map foreign-session collision surface.
  • next-surface-adjacency — W3 is Next multipage. Does anything W2 builds (the consume-and-parity pattern) generalize to a Next surface cheaply, or would coupling them now over-scope W2? Why: shape W2 so W3 is a small step, without pulling W3 work forward.

Scope guardrails (this wave)

  • Touch: js/ (@barkpark/react consumer wiring only if needed), a minimal test-only Astro surface under the parity harness, the EXISTING golden harness/comparator (reuse, extend only if a shim is unavoidable).
  • DO NOT touch: any api/**/*.ex (a live felix-pristine cycle owns api/; compose.ex is READ-ONLY source of truth); api/ + cloud/ connectors surface (#3531, foreign); deploy/site-deploy.sh, deploy/instance-deploy.sh, templates/astro-starter/** (foreign site-spawner session).
  • Do NOT re-author the block array or any golden — the golden mirror is canonical; the Elixir emitter is the 1:1 target.
  • Model: every phase + every builder on Opus. Never Fable, never Haiku. Builders commit to LOCAL worktree branches off origin/main and do NOT push; the steward pushes + opens PRs. JS PRs merge on their own Node/JS gate.

This Paper is the wave's living story. Digest appends the survey digest + verify plan before the verifiers fly; Decide appends decisions + the wave plan before the builders fly; Review closes it as the debrief.

Digest — survey folded, verify fleet armed (2026-07-16)

15 surveyors returned. This section folds their evidence, states what is now established, flags the one contradiction that matters, maps coverage (found AND not-found), then names the verify fleet flying before Decide cuts the plan.

What the survey established (high confidence, file:line-backed)

  • The consume seam is real and was designed in W1. renderPortableDocument(value: Block[]): string (js/packages/react/src/PortableDoc.tsx:55) is a pure, framework-free string emitter returning bare block markup with NO .bp-paper-surface wrapper — its JSDoc (lines 49-54) literally names the Astro set:html use case. Exported from both index.ts:22 and server.ts:37 (RSC-safe).
  • Goldens + comparator reuse AS-IS. 42 pd-golden/*.golden.json fixtures, one uniform 5-key schema (_comment/type/input/expectedHtml/shape), Elixir-sourced (mix barkpark.portable_doc.gen_pd_parity), byte-identical across the api↔js mirror (diff -rq exit 0). tests/support/dom-shape.ts (assertShapeEqual/parseShape) is framework-agnostic and needs ZERO edits.
  • W2 is a genuine build, not verify-only. No .astro and no astro dep anywhere in js/; the only astro in-tree is the foreign, off-limits templates/astro-starter. No W2/Astro child task exists on the epic; no stale claims.
  • @astrojs/react is NOT needed (we inject a precomputed string, never hydrate a component) — but the BUILT shared chunk (dist/chunk-*.mjs:1) statically imports react + react/jsx-runtime, so the throwaway package MUST declare react (and react-dom for the peer decl) as a build-time devDep or astro build fails at import resolution. Never executed, never shipped.
  • Bundle-budget worry is moot. pnpm size only measures packages with a .size-limit.json; a test-only package has none. Under set:html with no client directive nothing ships — the correct deliverable is a first-class PROOF of zero shipped JS, not a byte budget.
  • CSS path is unblocked. @barkpark/react/paper-surface.css is an unconditional exports subpath to a self-contained (0 @import, 0 url()) 75KB asset; import it in the Astro surface for visual fidelity. Do NOT assert byte-identity on Astro's emitted CSS (Vite minifies/hashes it) — only that a <link> lands.
  • Placement + gate. Put the package at js/packages/astro-parity, mark it "private": true (the ONLY thing that stops publish; changesets auto-ignores private). .github/workflows/js-tests.yml (bare pnpm build + pnpm test via turbo) reaches it on the js/** path filter with no workflow edit. The Elixir gate fires on every PR but is harmless/irrelevant here. CAVEAT: adding an astro devDep mutates pnpm-lock.yaml — the committed lockfile MUST be regenerated or --frozen-lockfile breaks install repo-wide.

The one contradiction that matters (resolved by distinguishing two layers)

Two surveyors read like they disagree; they do not — they speak to different layers, and Decide must carry BOTH:

  • MUTATION layer (astro-html-fidelity): Astro does NOT reshape set:html-injected DOM. set:html is opaque/verbatim; compressHTML:true only collapses whitespace, which the comparator already normalizes; both sides re-parse through the same happy-dom so any spec-normalization cancels. No normalization shim needed. (Asserted from documented semantics — Astro was never actually run.)
  • EXTRACTION layer (comparator-reuse-fit, EMPIRICALLY probed): the comparator is a FRAGMENT parser (body.innerHTML=). Feeding a full built page hoists head children → 5 roots, reds every compare. So a ~3-5 line harness-side shim IS unavoidable: parse the built .html as a FULL DOCUMENT (document.write/DOMParser, never innerHTML), querySelector the per-block container, pass its .outerHTML into the UNCHANGED assertShapeEqual(..., {unwrapClass:'bp-paper-surface'}). This does NOT modify dom-shape.ts.

Corollary that drives the test-page design: each golden is ONE block. So the Astro page must render each block in its OWN tagged container (e.g. <div class="bp-paper-surface" data-pd-type="paragraph" set:html=...>) so the shim can select 1:1 per fixture — a build-surface authoring requirement, not a comparator change.

The load-bearing UNKNOWN (why the fleet exists)

Every surveyor flagged the same gap: astro is installed nowhere, so the central W2 thesis — "does a real astro build (default compressHTML:true) pass set:html output through with unchanged DOM shape, and emit ZERO client JS?" — was reasoned, never RUN. The charter also pins the fictional astro ^7.0.0; the true installable version and whether experimental_AstroContainer exists there are unknown. The verify round's job is to STAND UP a throwaway astro build and prove the whole chain end-to-end.

Coverage map

Checked and FOUND (settled — do not re-litigate)

  • renderPortableDocument purity/exports/bare-markup — PortableDoc.tsx:55, index.ts:22, server.ts:37
  • 42 goldens uniform schema + api↔js byte-identical mirror (diff exit 0)
  • dom-shape.ts comparator framework-agnostic, 0 edits; unwrapClass affordance exists
  • W1 parity test pattern (renderToStaticMarkup → assertShapeEqual, unwrapClass)
  • built chunk statically imports react (build-time-only resolution dep)
  • @astrojs/react unnecessary; react-dom never on the string path
  • paper-surface.css exports subpath, self-contained, wrapper-selector match
  • workspace placement (packages/* glob), private:true publish guard, js-tests.yml gate reach, size-gate exclusion
  • Elixir gate fires on every PR but does not block js merge (merge-gates.md)
  • epic ledger: 10 children, 5 W1 done + 5 backlog, NO W2 task, no stale claims
  • EMPIRICAL happy-dom probe: full page → 5 roots; document.write+querySelector extracts cleanly

Checked and NOT FOUND (absences = decisions in waiting)

  • No astro anywhere in the tree — could not run astro build; the compressHTML-passthrough + zero-JS claims are UNPROVEN empirically. (THE gap.)
  • No existing zero-JS / no-hydration / astro-island assertion anywhere in repo — the zero-JS proof is net-new.
  • No production consumer of renderPortableDocument yet — the W2 surface is its FIRST real consumer.
  • Charter's astro ^7.0.0 is fictional — real installable version + experimental_AstroContainer presence UNVERIFIED.
  • Could not independently run mix test to reproduce the 42-golden freshness green (inferred from the blocking Elixir gate + merged #3513/#3514).
  • bp full-text search was unreachable to every surveyor (no bp search verb) — prior-art papers/tasks on astro parity were NOT queried; only the charter + tree were consulted.
  • bp task ls --all errored — a stray cross-epic astro task outside the epic children could not be programmatically ruled out (child_count reconciles 10/10, low risk).

Corners no surveyor reached

  • The design paper /papers/perfect-portabledoc-blog-next-astro-phoenix and issue #3382 (sub-path hosting) were never opened — W3 product detail is inferred from the charter one-liner only.
  • Turbo cache correctness for astro inputs outside tests/** globs (stale-hit risk) reasoned but not exercised.
  • CI-minute delta of a cold pnpm install + astro build (no pnpm-store cache in js-tests.yml) never measured.

Out-of-scope drift to record (NOT W2 work)

origin/main compose.ex now dispatches 3 new in-scope chat types (chat-approval:992, chat-question:996, chat-plan:1000, via #3514) with NO goldens; the manual-only scripts/pd-parity-completeness.sh would FAIL (count 45, 3 missing) but is NOT wired into CI. This is felix/api territory (compose.ex read-only for W2). W2 must NOT expand its type set to 45 — the 42 frozen goldens remain the target. Filed as a backlog note so a red guard is not mistaken for a W2 regression.

Verify fleet (in flight — all named, each with a RUN proof; results fold into Decide)

  1. [opus · worktree] astro-build-spike — THE central proof. Stand up a minimal test-only js/packages/astro-parity (private, react+react-dom+astro devDeps, no @astrojs/react), import renderPortableDocument + paper-surface.css, render a diverse subset (≥6: paragraph, heading, callout, divider, task-board [largest/nested], one chat type) each in its own data-pd-type-tagged .bp-paper-surface container via set:html (no client directive), run a REAL astro build, then a node/vitest script that (a) extracts each block via document.write+querySelector and asserts shape-equal vs the golden through the UNCHANGED dom-shape.ts; (b) globs dist/_astro/**/*.js asserting EMPTY; (c) greps built HTML for <astro-island asserting NONE; (d) adds a hydrating decoy page (client:load) and asserts the SAME checks turn RED on it (non-vacuous guard); (e) confirms a <link> to paper-surface.css lands in dist. RUN: pnpm install + astro build + the assertion script.
  2. [opus · worktree, same spike] harness+CI shape — from the spike worktree, confirm the operational contract Decide needs: does astro build FAIL if react is omitted; is the extraction shim exactly as predicted (document.write, not innerHTML); does pnpm install regenerate pnpm-lock.yaml cleanly; does pnpm size ignore the private package; does the package's test script need astro build && vitest (turbo test dependsOn ^build only). Report the resolved astro version.
  3. [sonnet] w1-parity-baseline — RUN the EXISTING W1 suite green to anchor the target: all 42 goldens still shape-equal to renderPortableDocument TODAY (exactly what the astro build must also equal). Distrust vacuous green: confirm it iterates 42 and the comparator self-proof (corrupted-node → red) fires. RUN: pnpm --filter @barkpark/react test.
  4. [sonnet] astro-version-and-container — settle the fictional-version gap and the full-build-vs-Container fork for Decide: what astro version actually installs, and does experimental_AstroContainer exist / is it still so named there. RUN: npm view astro version dist-tags and inspect the installed astro's astro/container export.

Decide will fold these results, then file the single W2 build task (suggested rpu-w2-astro-ssr-parity, parent portabledoc-blog-epic-goal, size M) and cut the build plan.

Decide (2026-07-16) — decisions cut, tasks filed, builders cleared to fly

Two explore rounds landed with ground truth in hand. The central W2 thesis was PROVEN empirically by the verify fleet (throwaway worktree, no commits, no main touch), the W1 anchor was re-run green, and the astro version/Container fork was settled. Below: what the proofs said, the decisions they forced, and the single-slice wave plan now in flight.

Verification results (proofs > facts > prose)

  • astro-build-spike — thesis PROVEN. A real astro build (output:"static", default compressHTML:true) passes renderPortableDocument() output injected via set:html through with DOM-shape UNCHANGED AND ships ZERO client JS. Decisive proof: 6 diverse goldens (paragraph, heading, callout, divider, task-board=largest/nested, chat-thinking) each extracted from the built dist/index.html and asserted through the UNCHANGED dom-shape.ts → Test Files 1 passed (1) | Tests 10 passed (10). Zero-JS: dist/_astro/**/*.js EMPTY, astro-island count: 0, only a paper-surface.css <link>. set:html bytes survive verbatim. Non-vacuous decoy: a client:load React island ships react/Counter/client .js and emits <astro-island> → SAME two checks RED (2/2 inverted green).
  • TWO findings that changed the plan. (1) LOAD-BEARING BLOCKER: astro build CRASHES out of the box — the js/package.json pnpm override "js-yaml@>=4.0.0 <4.2.0": ">=4.2.0" (no upper bound) resolves astro's js-yaml@^4.1.1 to js-yaml@5.1.0 (dropped the CJS default export) → "does not provide an export named 'default'". Cap to ">=4.2.0 <5.0.0" → js-yaml@4.3.0, build succeeds. (2) REFUTED digest claim: "the package MUST declare react+react-dom or astro build fails" is FALSE in-monorepo — react resolves transitively from @barkpark/react's own devDep; declaring stays correct hygiene (a PUBLISHED react-peer-only package WOULD fail), but not "fails without it".
  • w1-parity-baseline — anchor GREEN & non-vacuous. pnpm --filter @barkpark/react test = Test Files 10 passed (10) | Tests 185 passed (185); PortableDoc.parity.test.tsx = 59/59 ARMED (42 named fixtures + the 8-case corrupted-node protective proof firing red-on-corruption, 0 skipped). Mirrors byte-identical: diff -rq api/test/support/fixtures/pd-parity js/packages/react/tests/fixtures/pd-golden exit 0.
  • astro-version-and-container — fork settled. npm view astro version = 7.0.9 (real stable withastro/astro; the charter pins no version). experimental_AstroContainer exists in astro/container but is still experimental_-prefixed and skips the compressHTML build stage. RISK surfaced: astro 7.0.9 declares engines.node >=22.12.0 while js-tests.yml pins node 20 (two jobs) — unverified on node 20 → D23.

Coverage / not-founds: charter grep found NO astro version pin and NO AstroContainer mention (the "fictional ^7.0.0" was digest prose). No prior Astro-PortableDoc parity art exists (grep clean) — genuine build. The private spike packages are NOT size-measured. Epic ledger clean: 10 children, no pre-existing W2 task.

Decisions (each mirrors the charter — D16–D23)

  • D16 — full astro build is the parity gate, NOT experimental_AstroContainer. Why: honors the wish's literal "BUILD output" and is the only path proving compressHTML is shape-safe.
  • D17 — placement js/packages/astro-parity, private:true, no size script, own vitest.config.ts. Why: publish guard is private:true not the directory; a local vitest config or it inherits root browser/workerd projects and crashes.
  • D18 — the hydrating decoy is a SEPARATE package js/packages/astro-decoy (with @astrojs/react). Why: keeps @astrojs/react out of the parity path so zero-JS can't silently regress; its inverted assertions are the tripwire.
  • D19 — cap the js-yaml override to >=4.2.0 <5.0.0, commit the regenerated lockfile. Why: without it astro build cannot run in CI; the cap preserves the security intent and stays in astro's range.
  • D20 — dom-shape.ts stays 0-edit; a ~5-line full-document extraction shim bridges the built page. Why: set:html doesn't mutate DOM shape — only fragment extraction is real work, a harness shim not a comparator change.
  • D21 — the Astro page renders each block in its OWN data-pd-type-tagged .bp-paper-surface container, iterating the SAME 42 goldens, coverage>=42. Why: one surface with 42 children can't align to a single-block golden.
  • D22 — declare react+react-dom devDeps (hygiene) + link @barkpark/react/paper-surface.css; NO @astrojs/react. Why: correct against a published react-peer package at no runtime cost; CSS is the visual-fidelity deliverable, orthogonal to DOM-shape parity.
  • D23 — pin astro to a version whose engines admit node 20 (astro 5.x); do NOT bump the shared workflow's node. Why: the passthrough proof is version-robust — keep the shared CI file untouched to avoid cross-session blast radius.

Wave plan (in flight — 1 cohesive slice, opus)

W2 is one cohesive slice: the two private packages + the D19 reconciliation share js/package.json + js/pnpm-lock.yaml + the astro-parity vitest suite, so splitting would collide files. Filed and published under portabledoc-blog-epic-goal, linked to this Paper.

  • rpu-w2-astro-ssr-parity (surface: js/ — astro-parity + astro-decoy; builder: opus). Files: js/packages/astro-parity/, js/packages/astro-decoy/, js/package.json, js/pnpm-lock.yaml. Gate: cd js && pnpm install && pnpm --filter @barkpark/astro-parity build && pnpm --filter @barkpark/astro-parity test && pnpm --filter @barkpark/astro-decoy build && pnpm --filter @barkpark/astro-decoy test && pnpm --filter @barkpark/react test. 7 criteria (42-type parity, zero-JS proof, non-vacuous decoy, 0-edit comparator, js-yaml cap + node-20 build, W1 anchor still 185/185, merge-gated PR — lead closes on merge).

Backlog filed this wave

  • rpu-backlog-completeness-guard-chat-types (priority 3) — compose.ex now dispatches 3 new chat types (chat-approval/chat-question/chat-plan) with no goldens; the D8 completeness guard is red-if-run AND not CI-wired. Reconcile (add goldens or exclude) + wire the guard into CI. NOTE: api/ = felix territory; the 42 frozen W1 goldens stay unchanged and W2 must NOT expand to 45.

Pre-existing backlog children carried, NOT this wave: rpu-backlog-toplaintext-typekeyed, rpu-backlog-live-block-hydration (W4), rpu-backlog-field-embed-coverage (D7), rpu-backlog-role-ladder-drift-guard (D15), rpu-backlog-subpath-split-portabletext.

Review — debrief (2026-07-16): Wave 2 SHIPPED, grade A

Verdict: SHIPPED green, grade A. The independent reviewer re-ran the full slice gate end-to-end under nvm node v20.20.2 (mirroring js-tests.yml's pinned node 20) with a clean pnpm install: @barkpark/astro-parity build + 47 tests green, @barkpark/astro-decoy build + 4 tests green, @barkpark/react 185/185 (no regression from the js-yaml reconciliation). Zero code fixes were needed — the slice was correct, non-vacuous, and complete as built. Because nothing was fixed, the final integration branch is the builder's original branch, not an -r branch.

  • Zero shipped JS, on disk (D16). After a fresh build: find dist -name '*.js' | wc -l = 0; grep -c astro-island dist/index.html = 0; grep -o 'data-pd-type=' | wc -l = 42; the only shipped asset is dist/_astro/index.*.css (the paper-surface skin as a hashed <link>). Honest and complete. rpu-w2-astro-ssr-parity: criteria 0–5 stamped met with concrete, run-backed evidence AS the work happened; criterion 6 (“PR merged on the js gate”) correctly left met:false with empty evidence for the lead to close on merge; lifecycle in_progress (not done) — exactly right for done-but-unmerged. Parent, wave_paper, and assignee links all present. No not-green slices this wave. No other tasks touched. No ledger fixes required. The epic wave_status heartbeat was advanced to complete at review exit.

Grade — A

A. The wave does exactly what the wish asked, minimally and non-vacuously: it SSRs the canonical W1 renderer into a real Astro static build via set:html with zero hydration, then re-runs the EXISTING golden harness + comparator (0 edits) against Astro's BUILD output and proves DOM-shape parity for all 42 types — plus a first-class zero-JS proof and a separate hydrating decoy that keeps that proof honest. It reused everything it should (comparator, goldens, fixture array) and touched nothing it shouldn't (compose.ex and dom-shape.ts both 0-edit; the 42 frozen goldens were NOT expanded to the 45 that compose.ex now dispatches). The single load-bearing blocker (js-yaml) was reconciled with the safest possible cap. Bloat is near-zero: two tiny test-only packages, no shipped bytes.

Why not A+: two small hardening gaps a flawless wave would have closed. (1) The astro packages inherit turbo's global build inputs (src/**, tsup.config.ts, package.json, tsconfig.json) — which omit astro.config.mjs and the sibling react/tests/fixtures the page actually reads, so a local turbo cache could serve a stale dist and let the parity gate pass against stale HTML. Narrow (CI runners are cold → always fresh; fixtures are frozen), a developer-local DX smell rather than a gate-integrity failure, but a parity gate that can go stale-green is worth a per-package inputs override. (2) The astro packages define no typecheck/lint scripts, so turbo skips them — TS errors in the test/frontmatter surface only at vitest transpile / astro build. Both are notes for the lead, not blockers.

Next wave — W3 (Next multipage blog + basePath/assetPrefix)

The Astro consumption path is proven end-to-end. W3 (per the roadmap) builds the Next multipage blog — index + post pages — with sub-path hosting (basePath/assetPrefix, see #3382) and SEO/preview-manifest wiring, dropping the same PortableDoc renderer in. Reuse the golden harness + comparator as-is again; do NOT re-author the block array. Two backlog items the reviewer flags as increasingly worth pulling forward: (a) the compose.ex chat-type drift — it now dispatches chat-approval/chat-question/chat-plan with no goldens and the D8 completeness guard is red-if-run AND not CI-wired (reconcile via goldens-or-exclude + wire the guard; api/ is felix territory); (b) the PortableText-only consumer still pays for the ~16 KB renderer chunk (subpath-split if a Next consumer's bundle budget bites).
